guide.title: Steakhouses in Washington DC: Thirteen Rooms Inside the District
guide.destination: Washington DC Steakhouses, District of Columbia
guide.intro: Thirteen rooms, all of them inside the District, and eight stand within a ten-minute walk of each other downtown. The K Street power-dining corridor and the streets either side of it hold RARE on I Street, Morton's on Connecticut Avenue, Char Bar on L Street, the Palm on 19th, Bobby Van's on 15th, Joe's a block away on 15th, Mastro's on 13th and Fogo de Chão and the Capital Grille on Pennsylvania Avenue. Georgetown holds two more, Bourbon Steak in the Four Seasons on Pennsylvania Avenue and CUT in the Rosewood on 31st Street. The last two are out on their own: St. Anselm at Union Market and Medium Rare up Connecticut Avenue in Cleveland Park. Northern Virginia is a different page and is not this one.

sections.heading: The K Street corridor and downtown
sections.body:
Nine rooms in the blocks between Farragut Square and Pennsylvania Avenue, and the concentration is the reason this page did not have to leave the District.

RARE Steakhouse is at 1595 I Street NW, and it is the most explicit of them about method: the operator says a great steak is the foundation of the house and that this begins with the craftsmanship of its dry-aging program, run in climate-controlled aging rooms, with the beef butchered in house. USDA Prime dry-aged cuts sit alongside wagyu and a New Frontier bison ribeye, over four hundred wines behind them.

Morton's holds 1050 Connecticut Avenue NW, USDA prime aged beef in a room with a cigar-friendly lounge. Char Bar is at 2142 L Street NW, a kosher steakhouse under the supervision of the VAAD of Greater Washington, and it is the one room here whose menu runs wider than steak — kosher steaks first, then burgers, deli sandwiches and barbecue.

The Palm is at 1225 19th Street NW near Dupont Circle, Italian-inspired steaks and seafood with a sommelier on the floor. Two blocks of 15th Street carry two more: Bobby Van's Steakhouse at 809, prime dry-aged steaks and seafood, and Joe's Seafood, Prime Steak & Stone Crab at 750, steps from the White House. Bobby Van's also runs a larger sister room, the Grill, at 1201 New York Avenue NW, renovated in the autumn of 2018 with an atrium; it is not restated as a separate entry here.

Mastro's is at 600 13th Street NW in Penn Quarter, one block from Metro Center, with live music nightly and American, Australian and Japanese A5 wagyu beside bone-in ribeye and Kansas City strip. Fogo de Chão is at 1101 Pennsylvania Avenue NW over two levels, a churrascaria where Brazilian-trained gaucho chefs carve fire-roasted meats at the table. The Capital Grille is a few doors along at 601 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, and the operator's own locations list shows it is the only Capital Grille inside the District.

sections.heading: Georgetown
sections.body:
Two hotel steakhouses, four blocks apart, and both are chef-branded.

Bourbon Steak is at 2800 Pennsylvania Avenue NW inside the Four Seasons. Michael Mina calls it his love letter to the American steakhouse experience, classic Americana with his own flavors worked through it; there is a walled patio with fire pits and gardens behind the dining room, and a separate Bourbon Lounge.

CUT by Wolfgang Puck is at 1050 31st Street NW in the Rosewood, one of seven CUT restaurants worldwide. The room takes its cues from Georgetown around it, and a rooftop called CUT ABOVE sits over the main dining room and bar; Andrew Ho is executive chef.

sections.heading: Union Market and Cleveland Park
sections.body:
Two rooms a long way from K Street, and neither is a chophouse.

St. Anselm is at 1250 Fifth Street NE at Union Market. The operator files it as an American tavern rather than a steakhouse, built on live-fire cooking, with a menu that it says celebrates expertly prepared meats alongside seafood, vegetables and seasonal dishes. It is on this page because the fire and the meat are the center of the room, not a section of it — but it is a tavern with a grill, and reads like one.

Medium Rare is at 3500 Connecticut Avenue NW in Cleveland Park, and it sells one thing: a set menu of steak frites. Serving steak frites since 2011, per its own tagline, and the operator's other rooms are in Arlington, Bethesda, New Orleans and, soon, Baltimore and Columbia. This is the group's only room inside the District.

faq.question: Is this the District, or the District and Northern Virginia?
faq.answer: The District only. The rule this survey uses is to measure inside the city limits first and to extend outward only if the core cannot sustain a page on its own. Washington's core can: nine rooms sit within a short walk of the K Street corridor, with two more in Georgetown. Northern Virginia's steakhouse corridor through Tysons and Arlington is real and dense — Ruth's Chris, Fleming's, the Capital Grille, Fogo de Chão, Morton's, Eddie V's, 801 Chophouse, Oak Steakhouse and more — and it is dense enough to deserve a page of its own one day. Folding it in here would name the page Washington and then describe a suburb.

faq.question: What makes a room a steakhouse on this page?
faq.answer: Steak has to be the menu's center of gravity, plus the beef-centric genres — churrascaria, Argentine parrilla, Japanese wagyu counter, Korean-style beef room. In Washington that admits Fogo de Chão as a churrascaria, Medium Rare as a single-cut steak frites room, and St. Anselm as a live-fire meat house, and it admits Char Bar because kosher steaks are what it leads with. It excludes a restaurant that merely serves a good steak on an otherwise broad menu, and it excludes casual national chains entirely.

faq.question: Which rooms did this survey check and leave off?
faq.answer: Four. The Prime Rib's web address now redirects to an unrelated site and no source could be found placing the 2020 K Street room as trading. Charlie Palmer's own restaurant index lists Charlie Palmer Steak in New York and Reno, with no Washington room. Smith & Wollensky's own locations page lists thirteen restaurants worldwide and none of them is in Washington. And Medium Rare's own locations page gives one address inside the District, Cleveland Park, so the Capitol Hill room the survey counted collapses into it. A room whose status cannot be verified is left off rather than published with a hedge.

faq.question: How many Bobby Van's rooms are there?
faq.answer: Two in the District, and one of them is published here. Bobby Van's Steakhouse is at 809 15th Street NW, a block from McPherson Square; Bobby Van's Grill is the larger sister room at 1201 New York Avenue NW, with an atrium added in a 2018 renovation and seven private dining spaces. The survey that scoped this page named a single Bobby Van's at the 15th Street address, so the 15th Street room is the place and the Grill is named in the section above rather than repeated as an entry.

faq.question: Which of these rooms dry-age their own beef?
faq.answer: RARE Steakhouse is the one that documents it: climate-controlled aging rooms, beef butchered in house, USDA Prime dry-aged cuts and specialty cuts including wagyu and bison. Bobby Van's on 15th Street and Bobby Van's Grill on New York Avenue both describe themselves as specializing in prime dry-aged steaks, and Morton's serves USDA prime aged beef. None of them publishes how many days, so this page does not print a number.

photos.title: The 1500 block of K Street NW, Washington
photos.description: Looking east along K Street NW from 16th Street: eight- and nine-story office and hotel blocks in pale stone line both sidewalks, with a heavier limestone building carrying arched ground-floor openings at the right. A planted median divides the roadway, a white motorcoach and a Metrobus stand at the left curb, a dark sedan runs in the near lane, and cumulus cloud stands over the far end of the street.

places.name: RARE Steakhouse & Tavern
places.summary: RARE Steakhouse is at 1595 I Street NW, two blocks from the Metro and a short walk from the White House. The house runs climate-controlled aging rooms and butchers in house, and the list carries USDA Prime dry-aged cuts alongside wagyu and a New Frontier bison ribeye, with over four hundred wines behind them.

places.name: Morton's The Steakhouse
places.summary: Morton's downtown room is at 1050 Connecticut Avenue NW, serving USDA prime aged beef with fish and seafood beside it. A cigar-friendly lounge sits off the dining room, and private dining runs to the back.

places.name: Char Bar
places.summary: Char Bar is the kosher steakhouse at 2142 L Street NW, operating under the kosher supervision of the VAAD of Greater Washington. Kosher steaks lead the menu, with burgers, deli sandwiches and barbecue behind them, and mixed grill platters and brisket nachos in between.

places.name: The Palm
places.summary: The Palm's Washington room is at 1225 19th Street NW, a short walk from Dupont Circle, serving Italian-inspired steaks and seafood with a sommelier working the floor and private and semi-private dining off the main room.

places.name: Bobby Van's Steakhouse
places.summary: Bobby Van's Steakhouse is at 809 15th Street NW, a block from McPherson Square, specializing in prime dry-aged steaks and seafood. Lunch runs Monday to Friday and dinner nightly, with private dining for parties from twelve to sixty-five.

places.name: Joe's Seafood, Prime Steak & Stone Crab
places.summary: Joe's is at 750 15th Street NW, steps from the White House, serving prime steaks alongside Florida stone crab and the sides and Key lime pie the original room is known for.
places.history: The restaurant traces to Miami Beach in 1913, when Joseph and Jennie Weiss opened a casual dining spot that became known for stone crab. A partnership between the founding family and Richard Melman's Lettuce Entertain You in 2000 carried the name to Chicago, Las Vegas and Washington.

places.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
places.summary: Mastro's holds 600 13th Street NW in Penn Quarter, a block from Metro Center. Bone-in ribeye, Kansas City strip and American, Australian and Japanese A5 wagyu carry the list, and local musicians play nightly in the bar lounge.

places.name: Fogo de Chão
places.summary: The Penn Quarter churrascaria runs over two levels at 1101 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, with Brazilian-trained gaucho chefs carving fire-roasted steak, lamb, chicken and pork at the table. A market table of salads, cut vegetables, cured meats and imported cheeses stands in front of the grill.

places.name: The Capital Grille
places.summary: The Capital Grille's Washington steakhouse is at 601 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, between the Capitol and the White House, and the operator's own locations list shows it is the only room the chain runs inside the District.

places.name: Bourbon Steak
places.summary: Michael Mina's Washington steakhouse sits inside the Four Seasons at 2800 Pennsylvania Avenue NW in Georgetown. Mina describes it as his love letter to the American steakhouse experience; a walled patio with fire pits and gardens and a separate Bourbon Lounge run off the dining room.

places.name: CUT by Wolfgang Puck
places.summary: CUT is Wolfgang Puck's Washington steakhouse, in the Rosewood at 1050 31st Street NW in Georgetown, and one of seven CUT restaurants worldwide. A main dining room, a bar and lounge and a rooftop called CUT ABOVE share the building, with Andrew Ho as executive chef.

places.name: St. Anselm
places.summary: St. Anselm is at 1250 Fifth Street NE at Union Market, an American tavern built on live-fire cooking, and the butcher's steak is the plate the room is known for. The operator's own words are that the menu celebrates expertly prepared meats alongside seafood, vegetables and seasonal dishes, and the fire is what the room is arranged around.

places.name: Medium Rare
places.summary: Medium Rare is at 3500 Connecticut Avenue NW in Cleveland Park, and it serves a single set menu of steak frites — serving steak frites since 2011, per the operator's own tagline. It is the group's only room inside the District, with the others in Arlington, Bethesda, New Orleans, Columbia and Baltimore.

entries.name: RARE Steakhouse & Tavern
entries.note: 1595 I Street NW. The most documented dry-aging program on this page, run in the house's own aging rooms.

entries.name: Morton's The Steakhouse
entries.note: 1050 Connecticut Avenue NW. The lobby-bar half fills before the dining room does.

entries.name: Char Bar
entries.note: 2142 L Street NW. The District's kosher steakhouse; the mixed grill platter is the order to share.

entries.name: The Palm
entries.note: 1225 19th Street NW, near Dupont Circle. Caricatures on the walls and a sommelier who will find the bottle.

entries.name: Bobby Van's Steakhouse
entries.note: 809 15th Street NW. Prime dry-aged steaks a block from McPherson Square; the Grill on New York Avenue is the bigger sister room.

entries.name: Joe's Seafood, Prime Steak & Stone Crab
entries.note: 750 15th Street NW. Order the steak and the stone crab; the Key lime pie came with the name from Miami Beach.

entries.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
entries.note: 600 13th Street NW, Penn Quarter. Live music every night, and the wagyu list runs three countries deep.

entries.name: Fogo de Chão
entries.note: 1101 Pennsylvania Avenue NW. Two floors of rodizio service; start at the market table, not the skewers.

entries.name: The Capital Grille
entries.note: 601 Pennsylvania Avenue NW. The only room the chain runs inside the District, halfway between the Capitol and the White House.

entries.name: Bourbon Steak
entries.note: 2800 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, in the Four Seasons. Ask for the walled patio and the fire pits in shoulder season.

entries.name: CUT by Wolfgang Puck
entries.note: 1050 31st Street NW, in the Rosewood. CUT ABOVE on the roof takes the overflow and the drinks.

entries.name: St. Anselm
entries.note: 1250 Fifth Street NE, Union Market. A tavern with a fire in it rather than a chophouse — the butcher's steak is the plate.

entries.name: Medium Rare
entries.note: 3500 Connecticut Avenue NW. One set menu, steak frites, and no decision to make.
